questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. Dr Arvind Panagariya is its Chairman.
2. Its award period is from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
3. Its report was tabled in Parliament on 1 February 2026.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The members are T Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda and Soumya Kanti Ghosh.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the transfer of resources from the Union to the States, consider the following statements:
1. Article 270(1) deals with the sharing of the divisible pool of taxes on the recommendation of the Finance Commission.
2. Article 275(1) provides for grants-in-aid recommended by the Finance Commission.
3. Article 282 provides discretionary grants, mainly through Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The divisible pool excludes cesses, surcharges, taxes accruing to Union Territories and the cost of collection.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The 16th Finance Commission has recommended the vertical devolution of the divisible pool to the States at which one of the following levels?
questions.why: It is unchanged from the 15th Finance Commission, which had reduced it from the 42 per cent recommended by the 14th Commission. Cesses and surcharges remain outside the pool.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the horizontal devolution criteria of the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. Demographic performance is now based on population growth from 1971 to 2011.
2. The forest criterion now includes open forests, unlike the 15th Commission which counted only dense and moderate forests.
3. The tax and fiscal effort criterion was retained unchanged from the 15th Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The tax effort criterion was replaced by Contribution to GDP, worked out from the square root of a State's GSDP. Income distance is measured against the average of the top three large States, and population is based on the 2011 Census.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which one of the following is the basis of the 'Demographic Performance' criterion in the 16th Finance Commission?
opts: Change in the Total Fertility Rate over time
Population of the 2011 Census taken alone
Decadal growth of the urban population
questions.why: It replaced the Total Fertility Rate change used by the 15th Commission and rewards States with lower population growth, such as the southern States.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. Total grants-in-aid are Rs 9.47 lakh crore.
2. Rs 4.4 lakh crore is for rural local bodies and Rs 3.6 lakh crore for urban local bodies.
3. Revenue deficit grants have been continued as before.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Revenue deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants are discontinued. The urban share rose from 36% under the 15th Commission to 45%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to local body grants under the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. They are divided into 80% basic grants and 20% performance-based grants.
2. 50% of the basic grant is tied to sanitation, waste and water management.
3. Performance grants are fully tied to specific infrastructure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Performance grants are 100% untied. Funds are conditional on properly constituted local bodies, published audited accounts and timely State Finance Commissions.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the disaster management recommendations of the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. The corpus for the State Disaster Relief and Management Funds is Rs 2,04,401 crore.
2. The cost sharing is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 75:25 for others.
3. Heatwaves and lightning are recommended for notification as national disasters.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It also recommends upgrading the NDMIS into a comprehensive disaster management system for the Union and States.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the public finance reforms recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. The Centre should reduce its fiscal deficit to 3.5% of GDP by 2030-31.
2. States should cap the fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP.
3. It recommends review and closure of 308 inactive State public sector enterprises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It also asks States to stop off-budget borrowings, to set up SPVs for DISCOM debt, and to pursue privatisation of electricity DISCOMs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 16th Finance Commission recommends a Cabinet review of a State public sector enterprise that has made losses in how many of four consecutive years?
questions.why: The review decides whether to close it, privatise it or continue it for strategic reasons.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the definition of an urban settlement in the Census of India, consider the following statements:
1. The population of the settlement must be more than 5,000.
2. At least 75% of male employment must be non-agricultural.
3. The minimum density of population must be 400 persons per square kilometre.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Towns administratively classified as statutory towns are also counted as urban.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the urban announcements in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. City Economic Regions will be mapped, with Rs 5,000 crore allocated per region over five years.
2. A Rs 100 crore incentive is offered for a single municipal bond issue above Rs 1,000 crore.
3. Five university townships are proposed near industrial and logistics corridors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Funding is through a 'Challenge Mode', and the Urban Challenge Fund of Rs 1 lakh crore supports reform-driven urban projects.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Census definition shows India as less urban than studies using satellite data.
Statement-II: Satellite data of the Global Human Settlements Layer showed India as 63 per cent urban in 2015.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct. Census figures miss functional urban settlements outside municipal limits, for example Kerala is 47.7% urban by Census 2011 but about 80.8% by the DEGURBA method.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Annual Survey of India's City Systems (ASICS) is conducted by which one of the following?
opts: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.why: Its 2023 report suggests India may be far more urban than the Census indicates.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the challenges of Indian cities, consider the following statements:
1. Cities generate less than 0.6% of GDP as own-source revenue, against 2-4% in OECD countries.
2. Door-to-door waste collection has reached 98% of urban wards.
3. Low Floor Space Index norms raise land prices and the cost of infrastructure.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Segregation and processing of waste still lag, and cities lack a single chief executive with strong mayoral authority.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992, consider the following statements:
1. They added Part IX on Panchayats and Part IXA on Municipalities.
2. A three-tier structure is mandatory in States with a population of more than 20 lakh.
3. Fresh elections must be held within six months if a body is dissolved earlier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Elections are conducted by the State Election Commission and one-third of seats are reserved for women.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to local self-government in India, consider the following:
1. Panchayats have 29 functions in the Eleventh Schedule.
2. Municipalities have 18 functions in the Twelfth Schedule.
3. Part IX applies in full to Fifth Schedule Areas.
4. The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act was enacted in 1996.
How many of the above of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Part IX does not apply to Fifth Schedule areas directly, and was extended to them by the PESA Act, 1996.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to committees on Panchayati Raj, consider the following statements:
1. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) suggested a three-tier system.
2. The first Panchayati Raj Institution was formed at Nagaur in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959.
3. The Asoka Mehta Committee (1977) suggested a three-tier system with the Gram Panchayat as the base.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Asoka Mehta Committee suggested a two-tier system of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to rural decentralisation initiatives, consider the following statements:
1. The Devolution Index ranks States on framework, functions, finances, functionaries, capacity enhancement and accountability.
2. eGramSwaraj is integrated with the Government e-Marketplace.
3. SVAMITVA uses drone mapping to formalise rural property rights.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan is a revamped Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented since 2022-23.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the facts quoted on rural decentralisation, consider the following statements:
1. Women are about 40% of Panchayati Raj Institution leadership.
2. Fiscal decentralisation rose from about Rs 2.36 lakh crore under the 15th Commission to about Rs 4.35 lakh crore under the 16th.
3. The own-source revenue of Panchayats is above 30% of their total revenue.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: As per the RBI, own-source revenue of Panchayats is only 1.1% of their total revenue. The share of devolution rose from 39.9% in 2013-14 to 43.9% in 2021-22 on the Devolution Index.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It gives a legal entitlement of 125 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household a year.
2. It is one of the rural employment initiatives alongside DDU-GKY skilling.
3. It reduces the entitlement from 100 to 75 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The earlier ceiling was 100 days, which this law raises to 125 days.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the issue of 'freebies' in the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited v. Union of India case, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court raised concerns about the freebies culture in States.
2. The Court observed that undifferentiated cash transfers may disincentivise work.
3. The Court in 2013 in S. Subramaniam Balaji upheld distribution of colour TVs as consistent with the DPSPs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Court said indiscriminate largesse funded by taxpayers could undermine fiscal discipline.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Economic Survey 2025-26 on unconditional cash transfers, consider the following statements:
1. Spending on unconditional cash transfers, especially to women, is estimated at Rs 1.7 lakh crore in 2025-26.
2. The number of States running such schemes is projected to rise more than fivefold between 2022-23 and 2025-26.
3. Nearly half of those States are expected to face revenue surplus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Nearly half of such States are expected to face revenue deficits. The Survey contrasts 'Shreya', the enduring good such as capital expenditure, with 'Preya', the fleeting comfort.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to freebies and elections, consider the following statements:
1. Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 prohibits bribery of electors.
2. Election manifesto guidelines are part of the Model Code of Conduct.
3. The Supreme Court in S. Subramaniam Balaji (2013) held that distribution of freebies violates the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court upheld the distribution of items such as colour TVs and laptops as consistent with the DPSPs, but said States should open avenues for employment instead of non-merit freebies.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the combined gross fiscal deficit of States rose from 2.6% of GDP in 2021-22 to which one of the following in 2024-25?
questions.why: Freebies and unconditional transfers are among the factors strained by State finances.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the PM RAHAT scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It is a scheme of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
2. It provides cashless treatment up to Rs 1.5 lakh per accident victim for 7 days from the date of accident.
3. It covers road accident victims only on national highways.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It applies to victims on any category of road. Stabilisation treatment is up to 24 hours for non-life-threatening injuries and up to 48 hours for life-threatening ones.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the funding and monitoring of PM RAHAT, consider the following statements:
1. Hospitals are reimbursed through the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund.
2. Claims are to be paid within 10 days by the State Health Agency.
3. The State Road Safety Council is the nodal agency at the State level.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Uninsured and hit-and-run cases are paid from the Government of India's budget, and the scheme is linked with the 112 emergency number.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The 'RahVeer' under the PM RAHAT scheme refers to which one of the following?
questions.why: Accident victims or Good Samaritans can call 112 to reach the nearest hospital and ambulance support.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It is released annually by Transparency International.
2. India's rank improved from 96th to 91st with a score of 39.
3. Denmark ranked first for the eighth consecutive time with a score of 89.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. CPI scores run from 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean). Venezuela scored 10 and Somalia and South Sudan scored 9.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to what the Corruption Perceptions Index leaves out, consider the following statements:
1. Citizens' direct experience of corruption is not covered.
2. Private sector corruption is not covered.
3. Money laundering is not covered.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are excluded. The CPI is a composite of at least 3 and up to 13 surveys and assessments on perceived public sector corruption.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Public Trust Doctrine, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in India in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1996).
2. It holds that natural resources belong to the State in trust for the people.
3. It allows the State to sell natural resources freely for private exploitation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The doctrine says resources cannot be sold for private exploitation. Article 21, Article 51A(g) and Article 48A are linked to environmental protection.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the weakening of environmental protections discussed in the news, consider the following statements:
1. Since 18 December 2025, for non-coal mining projects, land acquisition can occur before an Environmental Impact Assessment.
2. The Court accepted a 100-metre height-based definition for the Aravalli hills.
3. The Vanashakti v. Union of India (2025) judgment was recalled, which diluted the ban on retrospective clearances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct as stated in the discussion. It argues these trends contradict Article 21 and the Public Trust Doctrine.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Gender Budget in India, consider the following statements:
1. India formally adopted gender budgeting in 2004-05.
2. The share of the Gender Budget in the Union Budget rose to 9.37%.
3. Part A of the Gender Budget covers schemes with at least 30% allocation for women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Part A covers schemes with 100% provision for women, and Part B covers schemes with at least 30%. The Gender Budgeting Scheme is under the Samarthya sub-scheme of Mission Shakti.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The discussion on the President's Address in the Lok Sabha takes place on a Motion of Thanks under which one of the following?
opts: Article 86(1) of the Constitution of India
Rule 17 of the Lok Sabha Rules
Rule 5 of the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure
Article 87(2) of the Constitution of India
questions.why: Article 87(1) says the President addresses both Houses at the first session after a general election and at the first session of each year. Opposition members may move amendments expressing regret.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the NOTA option in elections, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court directed the ECI to include NOTA on EVMs in PUCL v. Union of India (2013).
2. It was first implemented in 2013 in the assembly elections of Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.
3. If NOTA gets the highest votes, a fresh election is held under the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Even if NOTA gets the highest votes, the candidate with the next highest votes is declared the winner. The State Election Commissions of Maharashtra and Haryana treat NOTA as a fictional candidate and order re-elections if it secures a majority.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Article 3 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Parliament can form a new State or alter the boundaries or name of a State.
2. A bill needs the prior recommendation of the President.
3. A constitutional amendment under Article 368 is needed to change the name of a State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Article 368 is not needed, and a simple majority is enough. The President must refer the bill to the State Legislature for its views, but is not bound by them. The Union Cabinet approved the change from Kerala to Keralam.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority (FNTA), consider the following statements:
1. It covers the districts of Tuensang, Mon, Kiphire, Longleng, Noklak and Shamator.
2. 46 subjects are devolved to it.
3. It overrides the special provisions of Article 371(A) for Nagaland.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: FNTA does not affect Article 371(A). The agreement was signed between the Government of India, Nagaland and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation, an apex body of eight Naga tribes.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation (ENPO), a party to the FNTA agreement, represents how many recognised Naga tribes of six eastern districts?
questions.why: They are the Konyak, Sangtam, Chang, Khiamniungan, Yimkhiung, Tikhir, Phom and Sumi.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the strains on the global trading system, consider the following statements:
1. The Appellate Body of the WTO has become largely non-functional because the United States blocked the appointment of new judges.
2. The Doha Development Agenda, started in 2001, remains unfinished.
3. The WTO takes decisions by qualified majority voting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The WTO works on the consensus rule, which lets any single member block a decision. Reform proposals include moving to qualified majority voting for appointing Appellate Body members.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to green and digital trade barriers, consider the following statements:
1. The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is seen as a unilateral trade barrier by developing States like India.
2. The rise of blocs such as RCEP is said to threaten the universal multilateral system.
3. Friend-shoring means moving supply chains to countries that are geographically nearby.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Near-shoring means moving to geographically nearby countries, while friend-shoring means moving to allies.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the visit of the President of France to India, consider the following statements:
1. The partnership was elevated to a 'Special Global Strategic Partnership'.
2. An annual Foreign Ministers' Comprehensive Dialogue was set up to track the Horizon 2047 Roadmap.
3. The 2026 India-France Year of Innovation was jointly inaugurated.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Relations began in 1947, became a Strategic Partnership in 1998, and the Horizon 2047 roadmap was adopted in 2023.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the defence and industrial outcomes of the India-France visit, consider the following statements:
1. The H125 final assembly line of Tata and Airbus is India's first private-sector helicopter facility.
2. MRO hubs will be set up for LEAP and M-88 engines.
3. A joint venture of BEL and Safran will make HAMMER smart munitions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A Joint Advanced Technology Development Group was also formed for military technology supply chains.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-France relations, consider the following statements:
1. France is the 2nd largest supplier of defence equipment to India.
2. The two countries are co-presidents of the International Solar Alliance and the CDRI.
3. France is India's largest trading partner within the EU.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: France is India's 3rd largest trading partner in the EU after the Netherlands and Germany, with trade of Euro 12.67 billion in 2024-25. Exercises include Varuna (Navy) and FRINJEX (Army).

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-France cooperation, consider the following:
1. The TRISHNA satellite is a joint project of ISRO and CNES.
2. UPI has been launched in France.
3. France supports India's permanent seat in the UN Security Council.
4. France has no role in the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor.
How many of the above of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: France is a key stakeholder in IMEC.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-US trade agreement, consider the following statements:
1. US reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods were cut from 25% to 18%.
2. The US withdrew the additional 25% duty imposed over Russian oil imports.
3. India-US bilateral trade in FY25 was a record US$ 132.2 billion.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. In August 2025 the US had imposed up to 50% tariff comprising 25% reciprocal and an additional 25% duty.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-US trade relations, consider the following statements:
1. India runs a trade surplus with the US, driven mainly by services and high-value goods.
2. The US is the 3rd largest investor in India with cumulative FDI of US$ 70.65 billion from 2000 to 2025.
3. Crude oil, LNG and aircraft are key Indian exports to the US.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Crude oil, LNG, aircraft and parts and defence equipment are key US exports to India. India exports pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, electronics and gems and jewellery.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), consider the following statements:
1. It was established by an agreement concluded on 25 May 1981.
2. Its headquarters is at Riyadh.
3. Iran, Iraq and Yemen are among its six members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The six members are the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait. India-GCC trade was USD 178.56 billion in 2024-25, about 15.42% of India's global trade.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: A Framework Agreement on Economic Cooperation to explore an FTA between India and the GCC was signed in New Delhi in which one of the following years?
questions.why: The terms of reference for the India-GCC Free Trade Agreement have now been finalised. GCC countries have a GDP market of US$ 2.3 trillion.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Prime Minister's visit to Israel, consider the following statements:
1. Ties were upgraded to a 'Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation and Prosperity'.
2. A quota of up to 50,000 Indian workers over five years was agreed.
3. A new initiative on Critical and Emerging Technologies is led by the foreign ministers of the two countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The initiative is led by the National Security Advisors and covers AI, cybersecurity, semiconductors, quantum computing, biotechnology and space. An India-Israel Innovation Centre for Agriculture is also planned.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-Malaysia relations, consider the following statements:
1. Relations were elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2024.
2. The 5th edition of the joint military exercise Harimau Shakti was conducted.
3. A Strategic Affairs Working Group and a Su-30 Forum were established.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Malaysia also reaffirmed its commitment as a reliable palm oil supplier.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the visit of the President of Seychelles to India, consider the following statements:
1. Seychelles will become a full member of the Colombo Security Conclave.
2. Seychelles agreed to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure.
3. India announced a special economic package of USD 175 million.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Colombo Security Conclave comprises India, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, Maldives and Bangladesh, and Seychelles will also recognise the Indian Pharmacopoeia.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Which one of the following is described as being developed by India in Seychelles to boost maritime surveillance?
questions.why: Seychelles is a pillar of SAGAR and Vision MAHASAGAR and lies near the Mozambique Channel. India also deployed a Coastal Surveillance Radar System there.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-Brazil relations, consider the following statements:
1. The bilateral trade goal was revised from $20 billion to $30 billion by 2030.
2. Diplomatic relations were established in 1948 and upgraded to a Strategic Partnership in 2006.
3. Brazil is a co-founder of the Global Biofuel Alliance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. In 2025 bilateral trade grew by over 25% to USD 15.21 billion, and Brazil ratified the ISA Agreement in 2022.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Power Gap Index, consider the following statements:
1. It is derived from the Asia Power Index produced by the Lowy Institute of Australia.
2. The index ranks 27 countries and territories using 131 indicators.
3. India's power gap score of -4.0 in 2025 shows that India operates below its full strategic potential.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It was cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26 and covers eight thematic measures such as military capability, economic capability and diplomatic influence.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) and the Combined Maritime Forces (CMF), consider the following statements:
1. IONS is a voluntary forum of navies of the Indian Ocean Region established in 2008 on the initiative of the Indian Navy.
2. India took the first-ever command of Combined Task Force-154 under the CMF.
3. The CMF has 47 members and is a legally binding military alliance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The CMF is a voluntary multinational partnership, a coalition of the willing, to uphold the rules-based international order. CTF-154 is a multinational training task force.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the US initiatives on critical minerals, consider the following statements:
1. FORGE is the successor to the Minerals Security Partnership.
2. The inaugural Critical Minerals Ministerial was hosted in Washington DC with over 50 countries including India.
3. Project Vault is a purely private venture with no public participation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Project Vault is an independently governed public-private partnership that will buy and store critical minerals and rare earth elements as the U.S. Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the New START Treaty, consider the following statements:
1. It was signed in 2010 and entered into force in 2011.
2. It caps deployed strategic nuclear warheads of the US and Russia at 1,550 each.
3. It is described as the last legally binding bilateral nuclear arms control treaty between them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It also limits ICBMs, SLBMs and heavy bombers, and its expiry removes the last legal restraint on the two largest arsenals.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The US Department of Energy has removed the ALARA principle from its directives.
Statement-II: ALARA is based on the Linear No-Threshold model, which assumes any radiation dose carries some cancer risk.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct. ALARA says radiation exposure should be kept as low as reasonably achievable, and its removal risks higher worker exposure.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the NATO mission Arctic Sentry, consider the following statements:
1. It is led by Joint Force Command Norfolk.
2. It seeks to safeguard NATO members in the Arctic amid increased Russian activity and growing Chinese interest.
3. It is led by the US Pacific Command.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Joint Force Command Norfolk serves as a bridge between North America and Europe for NATO.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to places in the news, consider the following statements:
1. The Rafah crossing is the southernmost exit from Gaza and borders Egypt's Sinai Peninsula.
2. Donetsk and Luhansk are the two key regions of Donbas.
3. Diego Garcia is the largest island of the Chagos archipelago.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The UK signed an agreement in 2025 to return Chagos to Mauritius while keeping Diego Garcia on a 99-year lease, following a 2019 ICJ ruling.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the conflict in Sudan, consider the following statements:
1. Reports indicated signs of genocide in the siege of El-Fasher by a paramilitary group.
2. The Darfur region lies in the west of Sudan.
3. The Masalit, Zaghawa and Fur communities were among those affected.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Kordofan, with El Obeid as its capital, and the Blue Nile state are other regions affected.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Ease of Doing Business reforms in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Business Reforms Action Plan was launched in 2014 by the DPIIT.
2. The Regulatory Compliance Burden initiative was launched in 2020 and about 47,000 compliances were reduced in five years.
3. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 decriminalised 183 provisions under 42 Acts.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India ranked 63 in the World Bank's Doing Business Report 2019, an improvement of 79 ranks in five years.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to digital initiatives for business in India, consider the following statements:
1. The SPICe+ form consolidates 10 essential procedures including DIN, PAN, TAN and GSTIN.
2. The Unified Logistics Interface Platform integrates 35 or more systems for real-time cargo tracking.
3. MCA21 Version 3 is an AI-driven platform for registry services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The National Single Window System facilitates clearances and approvals and PM GatiShakti NMP uses spatial planning data to reduce logistics costs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the challenges to ease of doing business in India, consider the following statements:
1. Over 4.6 crore cases are pending and about Rs 25 lakh crore is stuck in commercial disputes.
2. Improvements have mostly helped large corporations that can adapt to systems like GST and e-invoicing.
3. Land is a Union subject with digitised titles already available everywhere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Land is a complex State subject with a lack of clear, digitised titles. Dispute resolution takes about 1,400 days against a global average of 400 days.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Unique Land Parcel Identification Number' (U-PIN) is described as which one of the following?
opts: A tax identification for farm incomes
A registry of mortgages on farm land
An index of land prices by district
questions.why: It is meant to create dispute-free digital titles and de-risk industrial land acquisition. The District Business Reform Action Plan (D-BRAP) shifts reforms to municipalities.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the manufacturing announcements in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. The outlay of the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme is increased from Rs 22,919 crore to Rs 40,000 crore.
2. Dedicated rare earth corridors are proposed in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
3. India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 focuses on fabrication, packaging and equipment.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Three plug-and-play chemical parks and a new Construction and Infrastructure Equipment scheme are also announced.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the support for labour-intensive and legacy industries in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. A scheme will revive 200 legacy industrial clusters.
2. Mega Textile Parks will be developed in challenge mode.
3. A Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund is created.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A Rs 2,000 crore top-up is also given to the Self-Reliant India Fund set up in 2021 for micro enterprises.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the tax and customs reforms in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. A 5-year tax exemption is proposed for non-residents supplying capital goods.
2. A deferred duty payment window is introduced for trusted manufacturers.
3. All customs duties on aircraft parts are raised to promote domestic manufacturing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Budget exempts basic customs duty on specified parts for making microwave ovens and aircraft components. A single digital window streamlines multi-agency cargo clearance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Budget moves India from strategic autonomy towards strategic indispensability.
Statement-II: Indispensability means India becomes a critical node in global value chains.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct. The text also notes that the smiling curve shows higher value in upstream activities like R&D and design and downstream activities like branding, while assembly in the middle earns less.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Biopharma SHAKTI scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It has an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore over five years.
2. It plans 3 new NIPERs and the upgrading of 7 existing ones.
3. It plans a network of over 1,000 accredited clinical trial sites.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It also proposes strengthening the CDSCO with a dedicated scientific review cadre. SHAKTI stands for Strategy for Healthcare Advancement through Knowledge, Technology and Innovation.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to biologics and biosimilars, consider the following statements:
1. Biologics are medicines made from natural and living sources such as cells and microorganisms.
2. Vaccines and blood components are included among biologics.
3. Biosimilars are chemically different copies with clinically meaningful differences from the reference product.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Biosimilars are highly similar to the reference biologic with no clinically meaningful differences.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's bioeconomy, consider the following statements:
1. It grew from USD 10 billion in 2014 to USD 165.7 billion in 2024.
2. It contributes 4.25% to national GDP.
3. BioPharma is the largest of its four subsectors with 47%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: BioIndustrial is the largest at 47%, followed by BioPharma at 35%, Bioresearch at 9% and BioAgri at 8%. The target is USD 300 billion by 2030.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the initiatives to boost biopharmaceuticals in India, consider the following statements:
1. The National Biopharma Mission is implemented by BIRAC under the Department of Biotechnology.
2. Three bulk drug parks are being developed in Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh with an outlay of Rs 3,000 crore.
3. 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route in brownfield pharmaceutical projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: 100% automatic FDI is for greenfield pharmaceutical projects, while brownfield projects are allowed up to 74% automatic. The PRIP scheme was launched in 2023.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: 'Evergreening' of patents refers to which one of the following?
opts: Granting compulsory licences for a patented drug
Extending a patent by minor drug modifications
Reviving an expired patent through a court
Registering the same drug in many countries
questions.why: Companies make minor, non-essential changes to brand-name drugs nearing expiry, which leads to costly patent battles.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the support for MSMEs in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. All CPSE purchases from MSMEs are to be settled through TReDS.
2. GeM is to be linked with TReDS to share government purchase data with financiers.
3. TReDS receivables are to be introduced as asset-backed securities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A credit guarantee support through CGTMSE will cover invoice discounting on TReDS, and Corporate Mitras will help MSMEs with compliance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: 'Corporate Mitras' announced for MSMEs are described as which one of the following?
opts: Bank officers appointed to sanction MSME loans
Foreign buyers' liaison agents for MSME exports
questions.why: ICAI, ICSI and ICMAI will design short modular courses to train them, especially in Tier-II and Tier-III towns.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), consider the following statements:
1. It is an electronic platform for financing trade receivables of MSMEs through multiple financiers.
2. Only MSMEs can participate as sellers.
3. It was set up by SEBI in 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was set up by the Reserve Bank of India in 2018. Buyers can be corporates, Government Departments and PSUs, and financiers include banks and NBFC-Factors.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the classification and economic role of MSMEs, consider the following statements:
1. MSMEs are the largest employer in India, ahead of agriculture.
2. Classification is based on investment in plant and machinery and annual turnover.
3. The Union Budget 2025-26 raised the investment limits by 2.5 times and turnover limits by 2 times from 1 April 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: MSMEs are the second-largest employer after agriculture. They number over 7.47 crore and employ more than 32.82 crore people.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the contribution of MSMEs as per the Economic Survey 2025-26, consider the following:
1. 31.1% of India's GDP
2. About 35.4% of the nation's manufacturing
3. 48.58% of India's total exports
4. 51% of enterprises located in rural areas
How many of the above of the above are correct statements?
questions.why: All four are as reported by the Survey. Only about 1.1% of Udyam-registered MSMEs are actually engaged in exports.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the issues faced by MSMEs, consider the following statements:
1. Access to finance is the biggest obstacle for 21.5% of MSMEs.
2. As of November 2023, 97.92% of registered MSMEs were micro-enterprises and only 0.01% were medium.
3. About 5.8% of Indian MSMEs introduce new products or services, compared with 24.9% in South Asia.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. This is the 'missing middle' phenomenon, where firms stay small and informal to remain under the regulatory radar.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the initiatives for MSMEs, consider the following statements:
1. The Udyam Registration Portal was launched in 2020 and registration is free and paperless.
2. The Udyam Assist Platform of 2023 brings informal micro enterprises into the formal fold.
3. The Public Procurement Policy mandates 25% annual procurement from micro and small enterprises by Central bodies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. RAMP is a World Bank-supported Central Sector Scheme and PM VISHWAKARMA covers artisans of 18 trades.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The MSME Champion Scheme has which one of the following sets of components?
opts: Rural, Women-Led and Youth-Led Enterprise Support
Capital, Land-Based and Skill-Based Enterprise Support
questions.why: The innovative component covers incubation, design and IPR.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the revised Startup Recognition Framework, consider the following statements:
1. The turnover limit is raised from Rs 100 crore to Rs 200 crore for any financial year.
2. The age limit is 10 years.
3. Multi-State and State Cooperative Societies are newly included as eligible entities.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The DPIIT is the recognising authority, and an entity formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business is not eligible.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to deep tech startups under the revised framework, consider the following statements:
1. They are required to spend little on research and development.
2. Deep tech startups have an age limit of 20 years.
3. Their turnover limit is Rs 300 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A high percentage of expenditure on R&D relative to revenue is one of the criteria. They own or create significant novel IP and face long development timelines.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 has a total corpus of which one of the following?
questions.why: It aims at deep tech and tech-driven manufacturing, early-growth founders and high-risk capital gaps.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Orange Economy, consider the following statements:
1. The term was coined by former Colombian President Iván Duque Márquez and Felipe Buitrago in 2013.
2. It excludes software and research and development.
3. It centres on industries that use creativity and intellectual capital as primary inputs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It includes AVGC, filmmaking, music, performing arts, architecture, design, fashion, crafts, software and R&D. Orange was chosen as it is linked to culture and creativity.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Union Budget 2026-27 announcements on the Orange Economy, consider the following statements:
1. India currently has seventeen National Institutes of Design.
2. AVGC content creator labs are to be set up in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges through the IICT, Mumbai.
3. A new National Institute of Design is proposed in the eastern region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India currently has seven NIDs, all institutes of national importance. The AVGC sector is projected to need 2 million professionals by 2030.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the importance of the creative economy for India, consider the following statements:
1. Creative exports rose by 20% in 2023-24 to more than USD 11 billion.
2. The sector supports over 10 million livelihoods.
3. About 25% of the viewership of Indian OTT content comes from overseas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India offers a 40 to 60% cost advantage in animation and VFX services.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to initiatives for the creative economy, consider the following statements:
1. The UN General Assembly declared 2021 as the International Year of Creative Economy for Sustainable Development.
2. The Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 introduced anti-piracy provisions with jail time and fines.
3. India Cine Hub is a single-window digital platform for film shooting permissions.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The IICT was unveiled in Mumbai in 2024 as the National Centre of Excellence for AVGC-XR, and WAVES is a convergence platform for the media and entertainment sectors.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the concept of an 'Entrepreneurial State' in the Economic Survey 2025-26, consider the following statements:
1. The term is borrowed from the economist Mariana Mazzucato.
2. The Survey links it to the idea of strategic indispensability.
3. The Survey suggests that retrospective scrutiny of decisions encourages risk taking by officials.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It lists retrospective scrutiny as a barrier because good-faith decisions get examined later through audits, vigilance and judicial review. The 2G spectrum case is cited as an example of policy paralysis.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the barriers to an Entrepreneurial State, consider the following statements:
1. Officials are more likely to face trouble for trying a new solution than for following an outdated procedure.
2. Temporary measures like subsidies can harden into permanent commitments.
3. The Survey notes that excessive disclosure under the RTI Act can chill candid discussion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The text points to Japan's model of 'fair accountability' and South Korea's bounded safe spaces for experimentation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It was developed by NITI Aayog.
2. It targets Rs 16.72 lakh crore over FY26 to FY30 from assets in 12 sectors.
3. NMP 1.0 had a target of Rs 6 lakh crore and achieved 89% of it.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. NMP 1.0 was introduced in 2021 and covered 13 sectors, and highways, railways, power, pipelines and telecom were 72% of its target.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to asset monetisation, consider the following statements:
1. The idea was first suggested by the Vijay Kelkar Committee in 2012.
2. It focuses on greenfield assets that do not yet exist.
3. It involves a licence or lease of a government asset to a private entity for a period under a concession agreement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It focuses on brownfield assets, which are existing assets. NMP 2.0 also considers core assets, and non-core assets only when further development is planned.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to asset monetisation models, consider the following:
1. Toll-Operate-Transfer
2. Operate-Maintain-Transfer
3. Rehabilitate-Operate-Maintain-Transfer
4. Real Estate Investment Trusts
How many of the above of the above are used as models for asset monetisation?
questions.why: All four are used. TOT gives investors a 15 to 30 year right in exchange for a lump sum, and InvITs and REITs are structured financing models.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which Ministry met only about 30 per cent of its revised target under the National Monetisation Pipeline 1.0?
opts: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
questions.why: This was cited as asymmetrical performance across sectors. In railways, train operations are still carried out by Indian Railways.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to female labour force participation in India, consider the following statements:
1. Claudia Goldin's U-curve says female participation rises steadily during early industrialisation.
2. The Economic Survey 2025-26 says raising FLFPR to about 55% by 2050 could be critical for high growth.
3. India slipped from 129 to 131 in the WEF Global Gender Gap Report 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The U-curve says participation drops during early industrialisation when women leave agriculture and rises again only when education crosses a threshold and service jobs expand. She won the Nobel Prize in 2023.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to barriers to women's employment, consider the following statements:
1. Women are 43% of STEM graduates but only about 27% of the STEM workforce.
2. Women spend 363 minutes a day on unpaid work against 123 minutes for men.
3. Women make up about 28% of platform economy workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A World Bank study of 2021 found 31% of women cited commuting as a barrier to working.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Labour Codes and women's employment, consider the following statements:
1. They prohibit women from working at night in all establishments.
2. They provide up to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave and 12 weeks for adoptive and commissioning mothers.
3. They promote creche facilities for children below six.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Night work for women is permitted in factories in around 22 States and UTs and in commercial establishments in 33. 17 States and UTs have removed bans on women in hazardous industries.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The 'SHe-Box' portal is associated with which one of the following?
opts: Skilling of women in rural areas through NRLM
Women's access to credit from commercial banks
Hostels for working women in industrial cities
questions.why: It is an initiative of the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The SHE-Mart initiative of Budget 2026-27 gives better markets to products of self-help groups and rural women.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Lakhpati Didi initiative, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2023 under DAY-NRLM of the Ministry of Rural Development.
2. The target of 3 crore Lakhpati Didis was achieved a year ahead of March 2027.
3. A new goal of 6 crore has been set for March 2029.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A Lakhpati Didi is an SHG woman with sustainable annual household income above Rs 1 lakh, an average of at least Rs 10,000 a month over four agricultural seasons or business cycles.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the criteria and support under the Lakhpati Didi initiative, consider the following statements:
1. The woman should be an SHG member who completed at least two years and availed the Community Investment Fund.
2. The Revolving Fund gives Rs 2.5 lakh per SHG.
3. She should practise at least two livelihood activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Revolving Fund gives Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000 per eligible SHG, and the Community Investment Fund gives up to Rs 2.5 lakh per SHG. Bank linkage gives collateral-free loans of up to Rs 20 lakh per SHG.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: What is the approximate level of non-performing assets on loans of SHGs after the expansion of Business Correspondent Sakhis, as reported by the Rural Development Ministry?
questions.why: BC Sakhis provide doorstep banking and improved credit access for SHGs. Project eShakti of NABARD promotes technology in SHG operations.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), consider the following statements:
1. It offers only a hybrid incentive and no turnover-linked incentive.
2. It is a scheme of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
3. Its outlay was increased to Rs 40,000 crore in Budget 2026-27.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It offers a turnover-linked incentive for 6 years with one optional gestation year, a capex incentive for 5 years and a hybrid incentive. Targets include display modules, camera modules and printed circuit board assemblies.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the challenges of the electronics industry in India, consider the following statements:
1. India is a net importer of core components, mainly from China, South Korea and Vietnam.
2. Manufacturing in India is 10-20% more expensive than in China, Vietnam or Mexico.
3. Global e-waste is set to reach 82 million tonnes by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India's own share of e-waste is expected to rise to about 5 million tonnes.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to policies for the electronics sector, consider the following statements:
1. SPECS offers a 25% financial incentive on capital expenditure.
2. The National Policy on Electronics was adopted in 2019.
3. Electronics manufacturing allows 49% FDI under the government route only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route and has attracted over USD 4 billion since FY2020-21. PLI covers 14 sectors, and the Semicon India Programme began in 2021.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the capital goods sector in India, consider the following statements:
1. Public capital expenditure in Budget 2026-27 rises by about 9% to Rs 12.2 lakh crore.
2. The sector contributes about 12% of manufacturing output.
3. Around 40% of capital goods are imported.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The market size is USD 92 billion and the production is USD 32 billion, and R&D investment of 0.9% of GDP is below the policy target of 2.8%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the capital goods policies, consider the following statements:
1. The National Capital Goods Policy, 2016 aimed to raise the manufacturing share from 12% to 20% by 2025.
2. A Draft National Capital Goods Policy 2025 has been formulated.
3. India became a permanent member of the Washington Accord on engineering studies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The 2016 policy could not achieve its objective. The Mahalanobis Model, the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan, prioritised heavy and basic industries.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Union Budget 2026-27 measures for capital goods, consider the following statements:
1. CPSEs will set up two automated hi-tech tool rooms.
2. The basic customs duty exemption on capital goods is extended to lithium-ion cell manufacturing for battery storage.
3. Rs 10,000 crore is allocated over five years for container manufacturing.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A new CIE scheme will promote advanced equipment such as lifts, fire-fighting gear and tunnel borers.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the textile sector in India, consider the following statements:
1. It contributes about 2% to GDP and 11% of manufacturing GVA.
2. India is the 6th largest exporter of textiles and apparel.
3. The USA and the EU together account for about 47% of textile and apparel exports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It is the second-largest employment generator and about 80% of the industry's capacity is with MSMEs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the integrated programme for textiles in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. It includes a National Fibre Scheme for domestic fibre self-reliance.
2. It includes the Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme to modernise traditional clusters.
3. It includes the Mahatma Gandhi Gram Swaraj initiative for khadi, handloom and handicrafts.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It also has a National Handloom and Handicraft Programme, a Tex-Eco Initiative and the Samarth 2.0 skilling programme.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The export obligation period for textile garments, footwear and leather products made with duty-free imported inputs was extended from 6 months to which one of the following?
questions.why: The extension gives greater flexibility to exporters.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to challenges of the textile industry, consider the following statements:
1. Over 90% of weaving units are in the unorganised sector.
2. A 50% US tariff on Indian goods is a recent geopolitical challenge.
3. The Kapas Kisan app and 'Kasturi Cotton Bharat' are meant to improve the transparency and acceptance of Indian cotton.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The India-EU FTA is expected to give zero-duty access to major markets.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to food grain storage in India, consider the following statements:
1. Record food grain production of 353.96 million tonnes was achieved in 2024-25 (Third Advance Estimates).
2. About 60-70% of food grain is stored in FCI godowns.
3. Storage capacity with FCI and State agencies for Central Pool grains was 917.83 lakh metric tonnes on 1 July 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Around 60-70% of food grain produced is stored at household level in traditional structures. FCI procures at MSP and builds buffer stocks.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to schemes for grain storage, consider the following statements:
1. The world's largest grain storage plan in the cooperative sector works at the district cooperative bank level.
2. The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund was launched in 2020.
3. Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure is a component of the Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The plan develops storage at the PACS level through convergence of schemes such as AIF and AMI. PACS-based decentralised storage was also recommended by the Ashok Dalwai Committee.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which one of the following committees recommended expanding the Negotiable Warehouse Receipt system and computerising storage management?
questions.why: The Committee of 2014 also suggested converting FCI's conventional storage into silos with private participation. The CAG audit of 2023 urged phasing out CAP (Covered and Plinth) storage.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Advance Pricing Agreements (APA) in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. IT services are consolidated into a single category with a uniform safe harbour margin.
2. The threshold for safe harbour eligibility is raised from Rs 300 crore to Rs 2,000 crore.
3. APA processes are to be completed within 2 years, extendable by 6 months.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. An APA is a pre-emptive arrangement between a taxpayer and tax authorities fixing the transfer pricing method in advance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the debt-to-GDP ratio, consider the following statements:
1. It is estimated at 55.6% of GDP in Budget Estimates 2026-27.
2. India is on track to reach 50 plus or minus 1 per cent by 2030-31.
3. It is being used as the primary policy target in place of the fiscal deficit target.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct as stated. The FRBM Act, 2003 guides fiscal policy towards a sustainable path.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), consider the following statements:
1. It is available to corporates and Hindu Undivided Families.
2. It was introduced in 2004 by the RBI.
3. Resident individuals including minors can remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is not available to corporates, partnership firms, HUFs and trusts. Gambling, lottery, trading and speculation are prohibited, and Budget 2026-27 cut the TCS rate for education and medical expenses.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), consider the following statements:
1. PACS are grass-root institutions of the short-term cooperative credit structure.
2. Multi-State PACS fall under Entry 44 of the Union List and are administered by the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies.
3. Single-State PACS fall under Entry 32 of the State List.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A common ERP-based national software is used for computerisation, and the National Cooperation Policy 2025 promotes membership for women and weaker sections.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to cooperative governance reforms, consider the following statements:
1. The Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 mandates representation of women and SC/ST members on boards.
2. Cooperative societies are a subject only of the Union List.
3. Model bye-laws allow PACS to work as multipurpose service centres such as PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Cooperative societies are a State subject at Entry 32 of the State List, and multi-State societies are in the Union List at Entry 44.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Integrated Farming Systems (IFS), consider the following statements:
1. It integrates crops, livestock, horticulture, fishery, poultry and apiary on a single farm unit.
2. About 89.4% of Indian farmers operate on landholdings smaller than 2 hectares.
3. The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture promotes location-specific IFS clusters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. IFS is capital-intensive, needs technical skills and is labour-intensive, and the AICRP on IFS operates in 25 States.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Namo Bharat Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS), consider the following statements:
1. It is the same as the metro, with stops at every kilometre.
2. It is a semi-high-speed commuter system of up to 180 km per hour.
3. The implementing agency is the National Capital Region Transport Corporation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It differs from a metro in serving longer distances with fewer stops at higher speed, and from conventional trains in giving high-frequency point-to-point regional travel. The Delhi-Meerut RRTS cuts travel time from 3 hours to 60 minutes.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPMs), consider the following statements:
1. Dedicated corridors will be developed in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
2. India imported 60-80% of REPMs by value from China during 2022-25.
3. The REPM Manufacturing Scheme has an outlay of Rs 7,280 crore with a capacity of 6,000 MTPA.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. REPM demand is expected to double by 2030, and the National Critical Minerals Mission builds the supply chain.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the chemical industry in India, consider the following statements:
1. Budget 2026-27 proposes three new chemical parks with Rs 600 crore.
2. The industry contributes about 7% to GDP.
3. India is the largest chemical producer in the world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is the 6th largest chemical producer globally and 3rd largest in Asia. R&D investment is only 0.7% against a global average of 2.3%.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to PRAHAAR, India's national counter-terrorism policy and strategy, consider the following statements:
1. It is India's first national counter-terrorism policy and strategy unveiled by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. It articulates a seven-pillar framework.
3. The National Security Guard is the nodal counter-terror force under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Multi Agency Centre and the Joint Task Force on Intelligence in the IB are the central platforms for intelligence sharing.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the laws and international cooperation under PRAHAAR, consider the following statements:
1. The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 are among the special laws mentioned.
2. Local police are not expected to play any role in responding to a terror attack.
3. India uses Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties and extradition treaties for cooperation with foreign partners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Local police are the first responders, assisted by specialised State and Central anti-terror forces. Recovery and resilience follows a whole-of-society approach.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Under PRAHAAR, which one of the following is the nodal national counter-terror force under the Ministry of Home Affairs?
questions.why: It assists State forces in responding to major terror attacks. The BPR&D and the NSG also lead specialised training.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to technology in border management, consider the following statements:
1. Stages II and III of the Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System are to cover about 1,955 km of vulnerable borders.
2. A Border Security Technology Oversight Authority is suggested to audit surveillance operations.
3. BOLD-QIT was a pilot project for the system.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Drone incursions, tunnels, unfenced terrain and cyber attacks are listed among the challenges. Israel's Smart Fence and the US's Integrated Fixed Towers are given as examples.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to military exercises in the news, consider the following statements:
1. Vayu Shakti is the Indian Navy's flagship firepower demonstration.
2. Exercise Khanjar is the annual bilateral exercise between India and Kyrgyzstan.
3. Exercise MILAN is a biennial multilateral naval exercise hosted by the Indian Navy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Vayu Shakti is the Indian Air Force's flagship firepower demonstration exercise. Dharma Guardian is held with the Japan Ground Self-Defence Force.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP), consider the following statements:
1. VVP-II covers the same northern border villages as VVP-I.
2. VVP-I was launched in 2023 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for select villages along the northern border.
3. VVP-II was approved in 2025 as a Central Sector Scheme covering villages on land borders of 15 States and 2 UTs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: VVP-II covers other international land borders and not the northern border already covered by VVP-I. The scheme saturates villages with all-weather roads, telecom, television connectivity and electrification.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to INS Anjadip, consider the following statements:
1. It is the third of 8 Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft.
2. It was built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers, Kolkata.
3. It carries the Hull Mounted Sonar Abhay.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It is named after Anjadip Island off Karwar and is meant for the littoral combat environment as a 'Dolphin Hunter'.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), consider the following statements:
1. Budget 2026-27 announced Rs 20,000 crore over five years for CCUS.
2. CCUS is not useful for sectors such as steel and cement.
3. NITI Aayog's report sets a target of 750 million tonnes per annum of CO2 capture, utilisation and storage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: CCUS is described as the only known technology for decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors like steel, cement, petrochemicals and fertilisers. It enables blue hydrogen using coal gasification with CCUS.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to storage of captured CO2, consider the following statements:
1. Enhanced Oil Recovery and Enhanced Coal Bed Methane Recovery are among the geological storage routes.
2. Saline aquifers and basalt are permanent storage options.
3. Injecting CO2 too forcefully can fracture rock and induce micro-earthquakes.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The costs of direct air capture are estimated at USD 400-800 per tonne, and storage data on pore space in India is limited.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The CarbFix project, cited as an example of using machine learning to predict CO2 injection impacts, is located in which one of the following countries?
questions.why: India could use hub and cluster models in the Krishna-Godavari Basin and Rajasthan, and the National Centre of Excellence in Carbon Capture and Utilization is at IIT Bombay.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's closing of its proceedings on polluted rivers, consider the following statements:
1. The Court transferred primary monitoring to the National Green Tribunal.
2. The Court reaffirmed that a clean environment is part of the right to life under Article 21.
3. In M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987) the Court restrained industries from releasing effluents into the Ganga until they set up treatment plants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Court had begun the suo motu proceedings in 2021.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the status of river pollution in India, consider the following statements:
1. The CPCB identified 296 polluted stretches on 271 rivers.
2. Only 62% of 2116 monitored locations met the BOD criterion of less than 3.0 mg/L for outdoor bathing.
3. The Central Water Commission found at least one metal beyond limit at 112 of 434 stations.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The reports are the CPCB's 'Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality - 2025' and the CWC's 'Status of Trace and Toxic Metals in Rivers of India, 2024'.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the issues in controlling river pollution in India, consider the following statements:
1. Only 69% of the funds allocated to the Namami Gange Programme were utilised up to 2024-25.
2. More than 60% of India's sewage flows into rivers without purification.
3. State Pollution Control Boards often fail to coordinate with local municipal authorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Leather tanneries in Kanpur and factories along the Yamuna are cited as examples of weak enforcement.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the legal framework for controlling river pollution, consider the following statements:
1. The Environment Protection Act, 1986 was repealed by the NGT Act.
2. The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 established the CPCB and the State Pollution Control Boards.
3. The NGT Act, 2010 provides fast-track resolution of environmental cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Environment Protection Act, 1986 empowers the Government to set pollution standards and regulate hazardous waste. The National River Conservation Plan is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, and Namami Gange began in 2014 after the Ganga Action Plan of 1986.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The National Water Quality Monitoring Network assessing the water quality of water resources was established by which one of the following?
opts: CPCB with State Pollution Control Boards
Central Water Commission with the Ministry of Jal Shakti
National Green Tribunal with the High Courts
NITI Aayog with the Ministry of Environment
questions.why: State Pollution Control Boards in States and Pollution Control Committees in UTs take part. The EU Water Framework Directive is cited as a basin-wide approach.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. Article 6.4 is a carbon crediting mechanism.
2. Article 6.2 provides accounting and reporting guidance for Parties.
3. Article 6.8 provides for market-based cooperation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Article 6.8 provides opportunities for non-market-based cooperation. The first credits under the Article 6.4 mechanism were approved for a project in Myanmar coordinated with the Republic of Korea.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Great Nicobar mega-infrastructure project, consider the following statements:
1. The NGT upheld its environmental clearance, noting its strategic importance.
2. It plans a transshipment port, a dual-use civil-military airport and a 450 MVA gas and solar power plant.
3. About 130 sq. km of tropical rainforest is to be diverted.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Concerns include the Shompen, a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group, and the use of single-season data in the EIA.

questions.subject: Geography
